RagShortTexts: On July 25, 1261, general Alexios Strategopoulos infiltrated Constantinople with 800 men,.

Variants.Content: Alexios Strategopoulos reached Constantinople in late July 1261 with a reconnaissance force of only about 800 men. Local Greek informants, the Thelematarioi, reported that the Venetian fleet was away attacking an island, so the seaward defences were thin. The Byzantines slipped through a neglected passage in the walls, overwhelmed the sentries, and opened a gate for the army outside. Venetian quarters were set alight, and Latin Emperor Baldwin II fled. The episode ended the Latin Empire of Constantinople, founded in 1204, and restored Byzantine rule under the Palaiologan house.

Eight hundred frontier troops achieved what fifty years of continental warfare could not. When Emperor Michael VIII processed through the Golden Gate behind the Hodegetria icon of the Virgin, tears of gratitude bathed the marble floors of Hagia Sophia.

The work that night was quiet and close. Sentries near the Pege Gate were dispatched with knives while they slept, and the men moved without torches until the valves swung open. One cough or one dropped buckle in a narrow lane would alert the whole column. By the time Venetian merchants smelled smoke, Byzantine banners were flying from the battlements.

Citizens filled the squares singing hymns in Greek! Fifty-seven years of Latin desecration was erased in a single glorious sunrise. The imperial bells rang out across the Bosporus: the Roman Empire lives again!
